newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian army apologises as jet sparks bush fire.
newsitem.headline: Belgian army apologises as jet sparks bush fire.

text.p: The Belgian army publicly apologised on Friday after an F-16 fighter plane apparently started a major bush fire during military exercises.

"Of course we're sorry this has happened," army spokesman Colonel Gilbert Hertoghe told BRTN radio. "It's not the first bush fire this year. Usually we can contain it quickly. Unfortunately this went a bit further than it usually does."

Some 350 hectares of bone-dry heathland were destroyed on Thursday after the jet fired into the ground during the exercise in an uninhabited military area. Inhabitants of nearby villages reacted angrily after the fire threatened a number of houses.
"They show up when the weather is dry. Why don't they come when it's raining?" one inhabitant said.
Belgium is suffering one of the longest droughts on record and this month alone the country has only received 0.2 inches of rainfall compared with the normal 2.1 inches.
